spans.text: ■FILE■ PACC76539820163287—Decrypting...
Samantha Shaw (2009-2062),
Formerly known as Yekaterina Vasilievna Petrovskaya.
In 2034, Petrovskaya was admitted to the Zhukovsky Air Force Engineering Academy.
In 2037, she obtained a Master of Science degree in Automation and Advanced Mechanical Engineering.

In the same year, she joined the Neo-Soviet Military as a technical expert as part of their recruitment program for top students from colleges and universities in relevant disciplines [Attachment 77].
In 2037, Sofya, a confirmed member of the Pandora Anti-Relic Organization, was arrested and imprisoned. Petrovskaya went to visit her at the prison [Attachment 81].
Decrypting Attachment 77...
Good afternoon, professors and fellow students. I am Yekaterina Vasilievna Petrovskaya.
As a graduate now with a degree in Automation and Advanced Mechanical Engineering, as well as the valedictorian of my cohort, it is my honor to pass on some of my experience to my underclassmen.
Those who know me know that I prefer spending my time alone in the lab tinkering with machinery to making pointless small talk with people.
But I can't avoid socializing all the time—launching a new research project requires funding, so to butter up my professors, here I am, rambling and talking your ear off.
I was born in Stavropol Krai, a place with lots of salt lakes, natural gas, and wild animals that shit everywhere.
But that did not dampen my love for aircraft.
I played with paper planes when I was little, and when I grew up, I wanted to play with real planes.
Teachers giving career advice when we're in school are always talking about our prospects, our talents, our dreams...
That's all a load of bull to me.
I didn't come to study at this academy for some noble reason. I'm not a particularly noble person to begin with.
I hate studying. It's torture.
I only persevered because I knew all this torture would eventually lead to something that brings me joy.
I can't imagine myself cooking for people in some hotel kitchen, that's for sure.
Speaking of which, there is a clear upside to being in my department—
The building is the closest to the cafeteria, so we're always the first to get to the food after class.
Decrypting Attachment 81...
Don't give me that long face, I'm not dead yet.
...You haven't come home in six years. We all thought you were dead.
Thank goodness you're still around. Mama and Papa must be so proud of you.
I hear you hold a military rank now, is that true? Then am I causing you any trouble?
...It doesn't matter, I don't really care where I go.
How did you get into this mess?
I wasn't coerced; I wasn't deceived; I wasn't brainwashed—I joined them voluntarily.
Why?
Humans shouldn't mess with Relic technology, just as a toddler shouldn't be given the launch key of the Tsar Bomba. It's too dangerous.
And kidnapping Relic Agency personnel isn't dangerous?
...We have no other choice.
"Relic Agency"? They're just a bunch of crooks profiteering under the guise of scientific research.
...You're such an idiot.
...I suppose you're right.
The Relic Agency won't abandon their research on the Relics just because they lost a few people.
...I know.
But I still wanted to do SOMETHING.
It might've been pointless, Katya, but it was the only right thing I could do.
That's why you're an idiot.
Just you wait, I'll show you the right way to go about it.
Katya, what...
Ma'am, your visiting time is up. Please take your leave.
...What are you planning to do?
You wait and see. I will prove to the world that we don't even need Relic technology.
